reasons: Emergency detection relies on phrase matching that can miss or over-trigger.
Only two behaviors are tested: emergency intercept and an ordinary question.
The ordinary-question test calls the real model when a key is set, so its result depends on the environment.
The OpenAI temperature setting is ignored here.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and the AI safety rules
sections.what: Loads the libraries and settings, then defines a long set of standing instructions. The instructions tell the AI to stay within the patient's records, avoid diagnosing or prescribing, cite sources, and write warmly.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the AI within clinical safety limits. The rules are written in the prompt itself.
sections.watch_out: Changing these rules changes the safety behavior of every reply, so review edits carefully.

sections.name: ChatbotEngine (part 1)
sections.title: Emergency phrase check
sections.what: Holds the list of urgent phrases, such as chest pain and trouble breathing, and defines the chatbot class with its main reply method. If a message contains any listed phrase, the reply is a fixed message telling the patient to call 112, and the AI is never called.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed safety response for urgent cases that does not depend on the AI being available.
sections.watch_out: The check is a plain text search, so spelling variations and other languages can slip past while words that merely contain a phrase can trigger it.

sections.name: ChatbotEngine (part 2)
sections.title: Building the records context and choosing a provider
sections.what: Turns the health profile and retrieved document excerpts into labelled text for the AI, and records a source entry for each excerpt so the reply can cite them. It then selects Groq if its key is set, or OpenAI if not.
sections.why: Likely reason: the AI can only ground its answer in what is passed to it. Reason for the snippet length of 160 characters is not stated.
sections.watch_out: Sources show a short snippet but the AI receives the full excerpt text, so long records increase cost and response time.

sections.name: ChatbotEngine (part 3)
sections.title: Template reply and message assembly
sections.what: If no AI key is set, returns a template reply that shows the start of the records text with a note that the service is in demonstration mode. Otherwise it builds the message list with recent history and the question with the records attached.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app run in demonstration mode without an AI key. The reason is stated in the note text.
sections.watch_out: The template reply shows the first 300 characters of raw record text, which may expose sensitive details on screen.

sections.name: ChatbotEngine (part 4)
sections.title: Calling the AI and suggestion chips
sections.what: Sends the messages to the chosen model with low randomness and a length cap, then returns the reply with sources and follow-up suggestions picked by keyword. If the call fails, it returns a safe apology instead of an error.
sections.why: Likely reason: a failed model call should not break the chat screen. The apology text is written in the code.
sections.watch_out: The apology is returned as a normal reply, so the app cannot tell a failure from a real answer without checking the logs.

summary: Writes the AI's replies to patient questions about their records, using a keyword check for emergencies and rules that keep answers within the patient's own documents.
purpose: Handles one chat message. It returns a fixed emergency message when needed, otherwise it builds context from the patient's records and asks an AI model for a reply.
why: Likely reason: patient safety. The emergency check runs before any AI call so urgent messages are never sent to the model. The reason for the grounding rules is stated in the prompt.
how: First it checks the message for emergency phrases and returns a fixed emergency message if any match. Otherwise it builds text from the health profile and retrieved document excerpts and records a source entry for each excerpt. It then picks Groq if its key is set, or OpenAI if not. If no key is set, it returns a template reply. Otherwise it sends the rules, recent history, and the question with the records to the model, and returns the reply, sources, and follow-up suggestions. Any model error returns a safe apology.
inputs: A user identifier, the message text, a session identifier, optional recent history, retrieved document excerpts, and a health profile with conditions, medications, vitals, and allergies.
outputs: A dictionary with the reply text and metadata: an emergency flag, sources, suggested follow-up questions, and the model name.
risks: Emergency detection is simple phrase matching. It can miss wording that is not on the list and can trigger on words that contain a listed phrase. The temperature is fixed in code. The no-key template reply includes the start of raw record text. The fallback apology hides the real cause of a failure.
debug: If an emergency reply does not appear, check the phrase list against the message. If replies ignore records, check that excerpts and the health profile reach this function. Logs record when a model call fails and why.
